models_evaluated: five commercially deployed chatbots (unnamed in text)

links.outcome: Reading level (FKGL) of chatbot responses to parents' paediatric health questions versus the AMA sixth-grade standard
links.effect: Median FKGL was 8.37 for chatbot responses versus 6.15 for parents' questions; 89.2% of chatbot responses exceeded the sixth-grade standard; every chatbot answered above the question's level (median difference +1.21 to +3.57 grades).
links.quote: The American Medical Association sixth-grade standard was exceeded by 99.3% of clinician-facing pages, 92.6% of family-facing pages and 89.2% of chatbot responses.

links.outcome: Change in reading-level gap when chatbots were explicitly instructed to answer at sixth-grade level
links.effect: With an explicit sixth-grade instruction, the median gap narrowed in every model and three of five models answered below the reader's level (100 questions, 1,500 responses).
links.quote: Given an explicit sixth-grade instruction, the median gap narrowed in every model and three of five answered below the reader's level.
